day: # Two years: Year One (cycle 1) begins on the First Sunday of Advent of an
# even-numbered year (2024, 2026 ...), Year Two (cycle 2) of an odd one (reading_cycle).
#   - Each day: two morning and two evening psalms (the second morning psalm a
#     laudate psalm, 145-150), an Old Testament reading, an epistle and a Gospel.
#     Readings from the Apocrypha come with the book's canonical alternative, after "or".
#   - 18-24 December are read by date, with the psalms of the day of the week;
#     25 December to 12 January by date (7-12 January only until the Baptism of
#     the Lord), the dated readings giving way to those of a Sunday after Christmas.
#     "Laudate Psalm" is the day of the week's (Sunday 150 ... Saturday 149).
#   - After the Baptism and after Pentecost, the weeks follow the Sunday's date
#     (Week following Sunday between Jan. 14 and 20 ...); those after the Baptism
#     stop at the Transfiguration, and the weekdays after the Day of Pentecost and
#     Trinity Sunday take the week their Sunday's date falls in.
#   - The eves (Christmas Eve, the Epiphany, the Baptism, the Ascension, Pentecost,
#     Trinity Sunday) are evening prayer only; where the book marks a reading for the
#     morning (*) or the evening (**) its kind says so (first_reading_morning ...).
#   - The Special Days (p. 1095), for both years, with the psalms of the day of the week.
# Typos in the table are corrected and listed in docs/source-errors.csv.
# Checked against the PC(USA)'s yearly lists for 2025 and 2026 (from the Book of
# Common Worship, 2018), which agree but for a few days: they give All Saints' Day
# its own psalms (96; 149 / 132; 134), the Epiphany Isaiah 52:7-13, 20 December
# (Year Two) Luke 1:26-36, and 2 Corinthians 13:1-13 for 13:1-14; an eve's
# psalms, listed here as their own evening, are there the day's Evening.
